fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'add that alongside our existing portability invariant as an agent guidance rule for this project: keeping rebar portable means it working across environments with diverse CI providers or no CI provider.'

Discovered via the compaction redesign: story A removed the operation-linked compaction trigger and story B replaced it with a GitHub-Actions-only schedule — silently breaking any adopter with no CI. rebar already has a portability invariant with real teeth: the blocking plan-review criterion `project.portability`, activated by `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and detected by the rubric `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`. Its `Platform and venue` matrix cell reads "macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD, CI, servers, developer workstations" — a single undifferentiated `CI` cell. Under it, a plan whose only trigger is GitHub Actions names a supported cell and draws no finding, because neither "a different CI provider" nor "no CI provider at all" is a nameable alternate shape. That is the gap this ticket closes.

## Approach
One authoritative wording, in the criterion's detection text; everything else points at it.

1. **Extend the criterion's detection text** — `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`:
   - split the `Platform and venue` matrix cell so both alternate shapes are nameable: "macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD, CI under any provider (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and others), projects with NO CI provider at all, servers, developer workstations."
   - add one rule under the matrix, in the rubric's existing cause-and-effect style, making the CI case concrete: a capability whose ONLY trigger is a specific CI system is not portable; a plan that schedules recurring or automatic work must state an operation-linked or in-process fallback, and a plan that does not is a finding whose alternate shape is "a project with no CI provider" and whose observable breakage is "the capability never runs at all."
   The finding threshold (all four elements) and the Non-findings guard are untouched, so silence about CI stays a non-finding and configured, opt-in CI behavior stays allowed — only a hard dependency fires.
2. **Pin the new detection text** — `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py::test_client_shape_matrix` asserts the `Platform and venue` value as an exact string, so it must carry the new value; add a sibling assertion that the no-CI-provider rule is present, so the rule cannot be silently dropped the way an unpinned paragraph could.
3. **Surface it where agents read** — `AGENTS.md` gains ONE bullet in the existing "Where to read (one-line pointers into `docs/`)" list, in that section's pointer style, naming the rule in a clause and pointing at `rebar explain project.portability` / `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`. No restatement of the rubric's full text — that file's own keep-it-lean rule forbids it.
4. **Regenerate, don't hand-edit** — `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the criteria registry; run `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` and commit whatever it produces.

**Deliberately out of scope.** `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` is pinned by `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` at exactly 8 cases with fixed ids (`PORT-F1..F4`, `PORT-N1..N4`) and `coverage_threshold: 1.0`; adding a ninth CI case would change the corpus contract and needs its own live `rebar criteria eval` attestation run. This ticket changes detection text only. `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md` is about the external LLM suite's provider matrix, not CI systems, and is not touched.

## Scope
- `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` — matrix cell + the no-CI-provider rule (the authoritative wording).
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` — pin the new matrix value and the new rule.
- `AGENTS.md` — one pointer bullet.
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — regenerated output.

## Testing
This is a rubric/guidance change, so the testable behavior is the pinned detection text, not new runtime code.
- **Happy path:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` passes with the new `Platform and venue` value, and the new assertion finds the no-CI-provider rule in the rubric body.
- **Failure path:** the new assertion is written against the rule's load-bearing phrase, so deleting the rule from the rubric fails the test — verified by removing the phrase locally and observing the failure before restoring it.
- **Unchanged contracts:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py` must pass untouched, proving the eval corpus contract and the `project-portability` coaching move are not disturbed.
- **Generator no-diff:** re-running the criteria-guide generator after the commit leaves the tree clean.
- **Gates:** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the `check_*` gates (`check_criteria_vocabulary.py` in particular, since it lints criterion wording), and the CI unit selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` names both "CI under any provider" and "projects with NO CI provider at all" in the `Platform and venue` matrix cell, and carries a rule stating that a capability whose only trigger is a specific CI system is not portable and requires an operation-linked or in-process fallback.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` pins both the new matrix value and the new rule, and passes.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` carries exactly one new bullet for the rule, in the existing one-line-pointer style, and restates no rubric text.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is regenerated (not hand-edited) and re-running the generator leaves the tree clean.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py` pass unchanged; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the CI unit selection are green.
